items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Nick Laney, the star football player at Duke was the leader. We got to Boston and there was a band there from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania... I also enrolled in Duke that fall.

ctx.x: We’re going to get to that, remind me, and I’ll ask you about that. Les Brown, Charlie Barnet? Were these the first let’s say name groups?

Well, go back to 1932. I had dropped out of school, and in North Carolina it was on a quarter system instead of the semester. I dropped out after the second quarter. And around Greensboro I just played with bands. And I think it was in May of that year I got a call from the leader of the Duke University Blue Devils band. They had two bands on the campus there. And this was before Les. And wanted to know if I would do a summer job with them in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, which I did, I took the job. And that band,…

school — into going to Duke that fall, which he did. And I also enrolled in Duke that fall. And I stayed there six weeks and left again. But Les graduated from Duke four years later. In the meantime I went back to Chapel Hill, ten miles away, at the University, the campus. And I was playing with Les’ band and also a campus band, and that was the end of my schooling after that. I wound up going to Chicago in 1936 with some fellows that I had met with the Biagini band in Savannah, Georgia, to Tybee Beach, Hank…
